title: Enterprise RAG Knowledge Assistant
subtitle: Lumina · documents, questions, and source-backed understanding
description: A document intelligence workspace with authenticated file ingestion, tenant-scoped BM25 retrieval, cited conversations, and a live Lumina product showcase.
status: Live product showcase · working local application
users: Teams exploring searchable document knowledge, cited answers, and an organization-scoped workspace.
challenges: The public Vercel deployment is a visual product tour with actual local application screenshots. Authentication, uploads, retrieval, and chat require the separately started local frontend and API.

The supported runtime uses lexical BM25 and SQLite. OpenAI or Ollama generation needs server configuration; dense/hybrid retrieval, enterprise SSO, and distributed production infrastructure remain roadmap work.

Lumina mobile workspace — responsive light-theme chat and conversation navigation; actual local app capture with fictional demo data.

architectureReference:
flowchart LR
  Visitor[Public visitor] --> Showcase[Vercel product tour + real captures]
  Workspace[Local Next.js workspace] --> API[FastAPI authenticated API]
  API --> Auth[Revocable sessions + organization scope]
  API --> Files[Validated PDF / DOCX / XLSX / text]
  Files --> Ingest[Extract + overlapping chunks]

  Search --> Store
  Search --> Answer[Extractive SSE / configured OpenAI or Ollama]

problem: Organizational documents become difficult to use when their knowledge is scattered and answers cannot be traced back to the original evidence.
solution: Bring files into an authenticated workspace, index their passages, retrieve organization-scoped evidence, and keep source citations attached to saved conversations.
technicalDetails: The supported FastAPI runtime validates uploads, extracts PDF/DOCX/XLSX/text content, builds overlapping chunks, and persists documents, sessions, conversations, and analytics in SQLite. Original uploads remain in local storage.

Tenant-filtered BM25 ranks actual source passages. Backend SSE carries response metadata, source excerpts, answer content, and completion status. Extractive mode works without a paid model; server-configured OpenAI or Ollama adapters enable generation.

The public Vercel product tour exposes four real application screens with fictional sample knowledge. It is deliberately separate from the authenticated local runtime and does not provide hosted upload or chat services.

caseStudy.architectureSummary: Lumina separates a publicly hosted Next.js product tour from its working local application. The local Next.js workspace calls a modular FastAPI runtime with revocable sessions and organization-scoped records. A single-process ingestion worker extracts validated files into overlapping chunks, SQLite persists workspace data, and BM25 retrieves tenant-filtered evidence for cited SSE responses. Server-configured OpenAI or Ollama can replace extractive answers with streamed generation.

features.title: Real document ingestion
features.description: Validate and parse PDF, DOCX, XLSX, and UTF-8 text, retain PDF page references, and create bounded overlapping chunks. Durable queued/extracting/chunking/indexed states support restart recovery and reindexing.

features.title: Tenant-scoped retrieval
features.description: BM25 ranks indexed passages using term frequency and document length, filtering both documents and chunks by the authenticated organization. Results carry document identity, page, excerpt, and relevance score.

features.title: Cited streaming conversations
features.description: The API streams metadata, sources, response content, and completion events while persisting messages and citation records. Conversations support rename/delete, and failures or cancellation retain explicit response status.

features.title: Authenticated organization workspace
features.description: Server-verified credentials, revocable sessions, organization-scoped records, administrator member controls, and audit entries replace the previous browser-only identity model.

features.title: Configurable AI generation
features.description: Start with explicitly labeled retrieved excerpts, then configure OpenAI or Ollama on the API server for evidence-grounded generation. Provider streams validate completion and surface errors instead of inventing a successful answer.

features.title: Live Lumina product tour
features.description: A public Vercel showcase lets visitors switch among real dashboard, library, chat, and mobile captures. It explains the local setup and clearly identifies the fictional sample documents and separate backend.

decisions.description: Deploy a polished product tour and real captures on Vercel, while keeping authenticated operations in the separately started local runtime.
decisions.tradeoff: Visitors can inspect the product immediately, but the public site does not run hosted file ingestion or chat.

decisions.title: Ground answers before adding generation
decisions.description: Tenant-filtered BM25 produces inspectable passages and extractive responses without requiring a model key.
decisions.tradeoff: Lexical retrieval is transparent and locally usable; dense/hybrid search remains planned, and optional LLM generation requires a configured provider.

decisions.tradeoff: This keeps local setup manageable; horizontal scaling needs a distributed queue, different persistence, and additional operational work.

Optional OpenAI/Ollama generation is configured only on the API server; extractive mode needs no model key.

solution: Use transactional booking, idempotency, signed QR admission, and optional asynchronous blockchain anchoring.
technicalDetails: Bookings and outbox writes share database transactions; conditional updates and idempotency prevent duplicate issuance and inventory overselling.
The worker leases outbox rows, renews ownership, and confirms anchoring through an adapter. SQLite supports local use while PostgreSQL provides the intended multi-replica database path.

caseStudy.architectureSummary: React calls Fastify for catalog, identity, booking, wallet, and admission workflows. SQLite enables local operation and PostgreSQL supplies the intended durable multi-replica data path. A transactional outbox lets a separate worker anchor private ticket commitments through an optional EVM registry.

title: RemoteShield X
subtitle: Secure remote-work browser
description: A desktop browser and administration toolkit with Tauri, a Node gateway, VPN checks, and mobile project assets.
users: Teams investigating controlled remote browsing and central network egress.
challenges: OS-level enforcement and VPN policy need deployment-specific validation. Source presence does not establish a security certification or support guarantee.
problem: Remote browsing policies depend on device, gateway, and network behavior working together.
solution: Combine a Tauri browser, VPN checks, and a central gateway for experiments with controlled browsing.
technicalDetails: The desktop source separates browser tabs, navigation, login, and VPN guards. The Node gateway separates authentication, admin, and proxy routes.
Networking and operating-system restrictions are deployment concerns in addition to application code. Their effectiveness must be tested on each supported platform.

caseStudy.architectureSummary: RemoteShield separates a Tauri/React desktop client, an Express gateway, PostgreSQL-backed session data, admin controls, and WireGuard/Nginx deployment configuration. A Flutter project provides a separate Android path.

features.title: Session and URL administration
features.description: Role-guarded routes inspect sessions, force logout, query IP logs, and manage blocked URLs; selected actions notify clients through Socket.io.

features.title: Gateway subnet policy
features.description: Outside configured development/test bypass modes, VPN middleware checks the request address against VPN_SUBNET.

challenges: Session storage is process-local; durable analysis history requires a persistent store. OpenAI features require server configuration.
problem: A resume lists skills, but does not directly explain how they fit a target role.
solution: Turn uploaded resume text into a skill graph and route the resulting context through analysis and generation endpoints.
technicalDetails: The upload flow parses PDF content before requesting analysis. The skill-analysis route returns graph nodes and edges for the interface.
Generation and prediction are separate routes sharing session context. Process-local session state makes persistence and deployment lifetime explicit trade-offs.

title: SolGuard AI
subtitle: Smart-contract audit research
description: A staged auditing prototype coordinating Solidity parsing, static checks, risk scoring, optional language-model reasoning, and patch suggestions.
users: Smart-contract developers reviewing candidate vulnerabilities and remediation suggestions.
challenges: The classifier can fall back to rules. Loading a base CodeBERT classifier does not demonstrate trained vulnerability accuracy, and generated patches require independent review.
architectureReference:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        SolGuard AI Platform                     │
│                                                                 │
│  Phase 1        Phase 2        Phase 3        Phase 4           │
│  Lexical    →   Neural    →   Semantic   →   Patching   →  XAI │
│  Observer       Auditor       Architect      Agent        UI    │
│                                                                 │
│  AST/CFG        GNN/BERT      LLM CoT        OpenZeppelin       │
│  Slither        SmartBugs     GPT-4/Claude   Foundry/HH         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
problem: Contract vulnerabilities need more context than a single lint warning provides.
solution: Coordinate static findings, risk scoring, reasoning, and proposed patches as inspectable stages.
technicalDetails: The orchestrator loads agents independently and records which phases complete. Static analysis results feed risk classification and subsequent reasoning.
The classifier explicitly records codebert or rule_based as its model source. Optional dependency availability and model quality are separate from simply displaying a confidence score.

caseStudy.architectureSummary: Python agents stage Solidity parsing, static findings, risk scoring, optional reasoning, and candidate patches. A separate React interface presents audit input, reports, and history; the published tree does not establish a fully connected browser-to-agent service.

title: AutoLedger AI
subtitle: Adaptive blockchain research

users: Developers exploring validator trust and adaptive network behavior.
architecture: simulated node state; separate PPO and ledger modules
challenges: The dashboard backend uses mock network state and random score changes. An integrated trained self-healing consensus network is not demonstrated by that feed.
problem: Validator behavior and trust changes are difficult to understand without a visible feedback loop.
solution: Explore trust scoring, consensus, and reinforcement-learning modules alongside a clearly simulated network dashboard.
technicalDetails: The FastAPI dashboard serves mock_network_state and changes node trust values on a WebSocket interval. It is a simulation rather than a production consensus feed.
A separate PyTorch actor-critic module samples actions and estimates values. Its presence does not establish that dashboard decisions are driven by a trained policy.

caseStudy.architectureSummary: The project separates blockchain/validator modules, trust/anomaly helpers, and a PPO actor-critic model. FastAPI publishes a simulated in-memory network feed to the React dashboard; that feed does not show a trained policy controlling real consensus.

title: AI-Adaptive Linux Scheduler
subtitle: Workload scheduling visualization
description: A full-stack simulation of process metrics and rule-based priority adjustments, visualized through a responsive monitoring dashboard.
users: Learners exploring CPU pressure, process priorities, and scheduler trade-offs.
challenges: The backend does not modify a real Linux scheduler or run a trained model. Its AI optimization label refers to deterministic threshold logic over simulated processes.
architectureReference:
graph TD;
    A[React/Vite Frontend] -->|REST API Calls| B[Node.js Backend]
    B -->|Generates| C[Process Metrics]
    B -->|Evaluates Load| D[AI Optimizer Module]
    D -->|Throttles| C
    C -->|Sends JSON| A
problem: CPU pressure and priority adjustments are easier to study when process behavior is visible.
solution: Simulate process metrics and threshold-driven throttling through an Express API and charting interface.
technicalDetails: The Express service keeps process and metric history in memory and periodically generates workload fluctuations.
Above an aggregate CPU threshold, selected non-root simulated processes have CPU values reduced and nice values raised. This is rule-based simulation rather than a kernel scheduler integration.

caseStudy.architectureSummary: Express keeps simulated process records and bounded CPU/memory history in memory, updates them on an interval, applies a high-load rule, and exposes JSON endpoints. React/Recharts displays the process and optimization behavior.

features.title: Threshold-based throttling
features.description: Above aggregate CPU load 85, up to three eligible heavy non-root records have simulated CPU usage reduced and nice values increased.

features.title: Bounded history and logs
features.description: The server retains a recent window of samples and optimization records instead of accumulating unbounded history.

features.title: Inspectable REST outputs
features.description: /api/metrics and /api/logs let the interface explain recent trends and which rule caused a priority change.

decisions.title: Keep the rule explainable

decisions.tradeoff: The demonstration changes in-memory values rather than Linux kernel priorities or a trained model policy.

decisions.title: Bound history in memory

decisions.tradeoff: The demo stays lightweight, but restarting the service loses its history.
